thread:
Ashwin: FYI our p99 on mixtral-10b-moex bumped ~25% in us-east after yesterday's batching/selector rollout. Root cause looks like a combo of RoPE scaling + kernel choice + router hot-swap.

Marta: which rollouts exactly? kernel-selector + adaptive batching?

Ashwin: yes. kernel-selector v1.5 (prefers cuBLAS for seq>256), batching window widened (max_wait_ms from 8->20). Repro on canary cluster shows worst at seq 200-480.

Nick: do we have micro-profiles? especially AES/KV allocs and router logits distribution.

Ashwin: pasted short flame summary from a reproducible trace:
```
hotspots:
  36.4% attention_kernel.cu:fast_path (cuBLAS)
  22.1% kv_cache_manage.cu:evict_loop
  14.0% router_logits_softmax.cu:topk_select
  9.5% expert_scatter_gather.cu
  rest ~18% miscellaneous (cuda memcpy, scheduling overhead)
```

Olivia: suspect RoPE scale interaction: Mixtral's head_dim and kv_dim ratio means attention kernel memory working set larger when RoPE scaling enabled -> triggers cuBLAS tiled path which allocs temp buffers.

Marta: are we seeing higher device malloc/free churn?

Ashwin: yes -- device mallocs/sec + peak mem increased ~40% for those mixed-length batches. KV cache suffered LRU churn since per-expert cache entries got evicted mid-request.

Nick: that explains router cost: cold experts => more dispatch + larger scatter/gather overhead. Also the router logits tail looks wider. Any change to router temperature/top_k recently?

Ashwin: router tweak last month: increased top_k default from 16->48 for better quality. That increases the number of experts we touch and amplifies cache pressure.

Olivia: quick experiments I ran locally:
- forcing attention_kernel=custom_fp16 (our fused attention) keeps peak mem ~stable and p99 down 20%
- reducing top_k to 12 reduces dispatch ops and cache misses significantly
- increasing per-expert cache entries by 2x mitigates evictions but raises overall memory footprint

ML-Evals: lowering top_k to 12 on small eval suite changed accuracy <0.4% on avg but some edge prompts degrade. Need broader eval before widescale.

Marta: options prioritized (low risk -> high risk): 1) per-batch kernel gating (choose fused attention unless >T% long seq), 2) conservative top_k rollback for MoE families, 3) bump expert cache allocation per-host, 4) revert batching window.

Nick: per-batch gating seems low risk. Implementation idea: compute batch seq histogram at enqueue time; if long_seq_pct < 30% pick fused path, else cuBLAS. Also add a kernel_fallback heuristic: if device_allocs/sec > threshold for 3s, switch to fused for next N batches.

Ashwin: I can implement gating + fallback and roll canary to us-east-1. Will include metrics: device_allocs/sec, kv_eviction_rate, router_unique_experts/tick, p95/p99.

Olivia: also propose adding a lightweight router metric: avg_topk_entropy per-batch to detect when top_k is mostly wasting slots (low entropy -> lower effective fanout).

Marta: good idea. infra team: can you prepare canary bucket and extended trace collection? InfraBot: will create canary job.

InfraBot: canary job created: canary-id cny-4107, starts 2026-03-18T11:20:00Z. Trace retention=120s. Alerts wired for kv_eviction_rate>0.15 and p99>1.2x baseline.

Nick: timeline: Ashwin to PR gating by EOD, canary run 2 hours, ML-Evals runs on full prompt suite in parallel, if QoQ <0.5% change then promote.

ML-Evals: we'll run the full dataset; ETA 4 hours after canary metrics stable.

Ashwin: starting PR. Quick note: RoPE scaling parameter we recently exposed (rope_scale_mul) interacts badly with fused kernel tiling. We should blacklist that kernel for configs with rope_scale_mul!=1 until we validate. Will add to PR.

Marta: good. Followups: 1) add kernel blacklist for rope scaling non-default, 2) add per-batch kernel gating + fallback, 3) run top_k A/B and expert cache sizing experiments. Sync 30m after canary starts. :thumbsup:
